svg.metadata: {"concept_id": "edu.diagonal-midpoint-bisection-comparison", "profiles": ["swell-paper-v1", "index-embossed-v1", "viewplus-variable-height-v1"], "teaching": "Compare the two physical quadrilateral models and measure or fold their diagonals. In the upper parallelogram both diagonals meet at their midpoints (equal halves). In the lower trapezoid the intersection divides each diagonal2:1, so they do not bisect each other. Both examples have1440square-mm area, but area equality is not the defining comparison. The lines join vertices and their shared intersection intentionally; this does not assert angle bisection. No endpoint letters, numerals or source theorem labels are drawn. Physical exploration and recognition remain pending.", "geometry_exception": "Swell and ViewPlus share1.4mm boundaries,1mm references/diagonals and explicit dashed circle references. Native1.2mm Index dots follow the logical graph with single junction dots and recorded corner guards; circle reference dots are sparser than perimeter dots. All alternatives remain in the same master. No exact source reconstruction.", "physical_evaluation": "pending"}

g.data-exception-reason: Native1.2mm graphic dots, not Braille. All vertices and intersections retain a single logical dot. Circle-reference sampling is sparser; polygon/diagonal junction guards and measured all-pairs clearance are explicit alternatives. Physical continuity remains pending.
